title: FM Sitharaman To Review Progress Of 'One State - One Regional Rural Bank' On May 6
summary: India's Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman will review progress on the 'One State - One Regional Rural Bank' initiative on May 6. The meeting is expected to assess consolidation timelines, implementation challenges, and steps to strengthen rural credit delivery by consolidating multiple regional rural banks into a single state-level entity.
content:
India's Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman is scheduled to review the progress of the 'One State - One Regional Rural Bank' initiative on May 6. The review will bring together officials from the Ministry of Finance, regulators, sponsor banks and state representatives to assess the pace of consolidation and remaining implementation tasks.

The 'One State - One Regional Rural Bank' approach aims to merge multiple regional rural banks (RRBs) operating within a state into a single, larger entity. Proponents say consolidation can improve operational efficiency, broaden balance sheets, simplify governance, and accelerate technology adoption, helping RRBs better serve agricultural and rural credit needs.

Key topics likely to feature in the review include merger timelines, regulatory approvals, capital support requirements, IT and core banking integration, staff rationalisation and redeployment plans, and measures to ensure uninterrupted credit flow to farmers and small borrowers during transitions.

Stakeholders in the process include the Ministry of Finance, the Reserve Bank of India, the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), sponsor commercial banks, and state governments. Coordination among these bodies is critical to resolve issues such as legacy liabilities, branch rationalisation and the legal aspects of merging multiple entities.

Advocates argue that larger state-level RRBs will have stronger capital buffers and improved ability to underwrite larger loans, introduce digital services and reach more customers through expanded product suites. Critics and some local stakeholders have expressed concerns about potential job losses, dilution of local oversight and the risk that consolidation could lead to branch closures in remote areas unless explicitly addressed in implementation plans.

The May 6 meeting is expected to set out next steps and target milestones, including a schedule for remaining mergers, timelines for regulatory clearances, and measures to protect rural outreach. Officials are also likely to discuss monitoring mechanisms to track service delivery and credit flows during the transition period.

Observers will be watching for announcements on capital support, concrete timelines for pending mergers and guidance on managing staff and branch issues. The outcome of the review could shape how quickly consolidated RRBs are established and how effectively they serve rural credit needs.

As the government moves ahead with banking sector reforms that affect rural finance, the review by FM Sitharaman on May 6 will be a key checkpoint for assessing whether the 'One State - One Regional Rural Bank' policy is translating into actionable progress on the ground.
